Hi Marissa,

Thanks — this is great. Apologies for the slightly messy notes on the call; here are the numbers we track today and the ask from product: 

- Typical request: generate up to 512 tokens (mostly summaries / recommendations).
- Target p95 generation latency: <= 120 ms (our UX folks prefer sub-100ms but 120ms OK).
- Target p50: ~30 ms.
- Sustained throughput: ~100 requests/sec (steady state for pilot cohort).
- Burst capacity: up to ~400 requests/sec for 2–5 minute windows (end-of-shift syncs, scheduled jobs).
- Model: experimenting with 70B-class open model; we’re flexible on exact model as long as quality meets clinical prompts.
- Security: patient PHI will be present in a subset of calls; we prefer Dedicated/VPC long-term, but ok piloting Hosted if logs and data residency are addressed for PoC.

I attached the latency CSV we pull from our infra so you can see distribution across endpoints.

Questions:
1) Is the Hosted API likely to meet p95 <=120ms for 512-token gen at those qps?
2) If not, what Dedicated sizing would you recommend and rough monthly cost?

Happy to jump back on a quick call if that’s easier.

Best,

Hi all — quick technical read on the numbers and practical recommendation. Short answer: Hosted can probably meet your target for the PoC, but Dedicated is the safer choice for production if you need guaranteed throughput and SLAs. Details below.

Observations from the profile:
- 512-token generation targets at p95 <=120ms are aggressive but achievable on optimized inference stacks when using: optimized kernels, KV/prefix caching, and reasonably short beam/temperature generations. p50 ~30ms implies most requests are much smaller (or are cached).
- Sustained 100 qps is modest; the challenge is the 400 qps burst for 2–5 minutes. That’s where provisioning matters.

Hosted API (PoC path):
- Pros: fastest to stand up, low time-to-value. We can run a controlled load test in our hosted environment to validate p95/p50 for your prompts. We’ll use regional routing to minimize network RTT and enable prefix caching where appropriate.
- Cons: Hosted autoscaling may introduce brief degradation during very fast spikes if they exceed cold-start/autoscaler reaction windows; we do offer burst credits but not a dedicated GPU pool by default. For PHI, we can enable stricter retention controls and limited logging for PoC (we’ll coordinate with Logan on DPA/SLA language).

Dedicated capacity (production):
- Pros: reserved GPU pool (predictable concurrency), strict isolation, and SLA-backed latency/uptime. With a Dedicated pool sized for your peak (buffer for 400 qps bursts), p95 at or below 120ms is achievable consistently.
- Cons: higher committed cost vs hosted, and lead time for procurement/provisioning (we can shorten via a reserved pool onboarding).

Recommendation / next steps:
1) Pilot: run a 2–4 week Hosted PoC that uses your exact prompts and traffic profile. We’ll run a synthetic load test first to validate the configuration and then a shadowed run with real traffic. This will tell us if Hosted meets your p95 consistently.
2) If we see tail latency or autoscaler issues during burst windows, move to Dedicated and size for sustained 100 qps + burst headroom (~400 qps) — I can provide a sizing worksheet. Preliminary ballpark: a Dedicated pool with 4–6 high-throughput GPUs (quantized model variants) for 70B-class models; I’ll follow up with a formal quote.
3) Security: for the PoC we’ll enable tighter logs, short retention, and documented controls. Long term we can move you into a VPC-enabled Dedicated or Private deployment.

I’m attaching our short performance playbook and can run the initial load test as early as next week if you’re good with the PoC path.

-Vivek
